maria_support: Customer on org acme-prod seeing intermittent 401s and spikes in latency. They say they can't find a trace id in the UI. Asked what to send for an escalation.

sam_oncall: ok — first ask for a minimal repro: a curl that hits our API, the timestamp (local time), and any client logs. If they can't run curl, screenshots + a HAR export are fine.

maria_support: i sent that. they're non-technical. can we give exact steps to find the 'request ref' and debug token from console / mobile?

raj_eng: short checklist to paste to customer:
- Web / JS SDK: Open DevTools → Network → find the request to api.redwood.inference (or your proxy) → look for header "x-rdw-reqref" or "x-request-ref". Copy that value.
- Hosted Console: open the request entry in the Requests view → click "Copy debug token" or "Get debug token" (top-right). Paste the token (looks like dbg_abcdef123).
- Mobile (Android/iOS): check the app logs for "reqRef" or "RequestRef:" printed around the network call. If using an embedded webview, capture a HAR from the system browser or proxy.

raj_eng: Example curl they can run (replace TOKEN and REQREF if available):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-ref: REQREF_IF_PRESENT" \
  'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/outputs' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

raj_eng: If they can't execute commands, ask them to export a HAR from Chrome: DevTools → Network → right-click → "Save all as HAR with content". Attach the HAR and the approximate timestamp (including timezone).

nina_support: for 401s also ask them to paste the full Authorization header (they can redact the token body) and the response body. Often a proxy or CDN will strip the req header — ask them to check gateway/CDN logs too.

maria_support: also remind them to include the region (e.g., us-west-2), org-id, and whether they're on Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Routing and auth behavior can differ.

sam_oncall: quick note for eng: once we have the debug token or reqref we can join the request in our logs and share a matched log snippet. If no reqref is present in the request, look for upstream proxy traces.

maria_support: i'm going to send a very short template to the customer that they can copy/paste — keeping it non-technical. thx :thumbsup:

maria_support (to customer_ah): Hi! To help us escalate quickly please attach: 1) Screenshot of the error + time you saw it, 2) HAR file from your browser (instructions above), 3) If you can run a curl, paste the command output, 4) Debug token from the Console or the x-request-ref header value. If you need help generating the HAR i can walk you through screen-by-screen.

customer_ah: thanks — i can grab HAR and a screenshot. how do i find the debug token in the Console? i'm on the hosted dashboard.

maria_support: in the hosted Console go to Requests → click the failing request → click "Get debug token". It copies a string like dbg_abcdef123 to your clipboard. Paste that here.

raj_eng: once we have the debug token / reqref and HAR we'll link the request in our logs and return a short repro/handoff to eng. If you see no reqref header at all in the HAR, that usually means a proxy/edge stripped it — please also attach any CDN/proxy config or logs.

sam_oncall: pasteable customer-friendly snippet: "Please attach: 1) Screenshot + exact time (include timezone), 2) HAR file from browser, 3) If possible a curl that reproduces the call (we provided a sample), 4) Debug token from Console or the x-request-ref header value."

maria_support: sent. closing this internal thread unless they come back with files.

deploy-bot: deploy complete: support/escalation-helper v1.4
